alarms.name: BH.HLT.LT01.ALM_LOW
alarms.cause: CLT transfer stopped or HLT drawn down by strike and sparge
alarms.consequence: Steam jacket heats a low liquid level; next brew starts late
alarms.action: Check the CLT level and the HLT fill valve; refill before the next mash-in

alarms.name: BH.HLT.TT01.ALM_HIGH
alarms.cause: Steam valve stuck open or HLT temperature loop in manual
alarms.consequence: Liquor too hot for strike and sparge; tannin extraction and scald risk
alarms.action: Close the HLT steam valve and check the temperature loop mode

alarms.name: BH.MLT.TT01.ALM_DEVIATION
alarms.cause: Jacket steam valve fault, poor mixing, or wrong strike temperature
alarms.consequence: Wrong fermentability; beer misses its final gravity
alarms.action: Check the MLT steam valve and rake; adjust the step manually if needed

alarms.name: BH.MLT.PDT01.ALM_HIGH
alarms.cause: Grain bed compacted (stuck mash) or runoff faster than the bed allows
alarms.consequence: Runoff stops; long lauter and poor extract
alarms.action: Reduce runoff, raise the rake and cut the bed, then resume slowly
alarms.text: MLT false-bottom differential pressure: high alarm

alarms.name: BH.KTL.LT01.ALM_HIGH
alarms.cause: Over-collection during lauter or boil-over at the hot break
alarms.consequence: Hot wort overflows the kettle; scald hazard and product loss
alarms.action: Cut the kettle steam immediately and stop the runoff

alarms.name: BH.KO.TT02.ALM_DEVIATION
alarms.cause: Glycol trim valve fault, warm glycol, or CLT water too warm at stage 1
alarms.consequence: Yeast pitched at the wrong temperature; off-flavors or slow start
alarms.action: Slow the wort pump, check the stage-2 glycol valve and glycol supply
alarms.text: Knockout wort temperature (after stage 2): deviation alarm

alarms.name: BH.KO.AT01.ALM_LOW
alarms.cause: O2 mass-flow controller fault or empty O2 cylinder
alarms.consequence: Under-oxygenated wort; sluggish fermentation
alarms.action: Check the O2 supply and the mass-flow controller

alarms.name: CEL.FV101.TT01.ALM_DEVIATION
alarms.cause: Glycol valve stuck or failed, glycol supply too warm, or chiller fault
alarms.consequence: Off-flavors (esters, fusels) or a stalled fermentation; batch loss
alarms.action: Check the zone glycol valve and the glycol supply temperature; put the zone in manual if needed

alarms.name: CEL.FV101.TT01.ALM_HIGH
alarms.cause: Runaway fermentation heat with no cooling, or the setpoint profile entered wrongly
alarms.consequence: Yeast stress, fusel alcohols, and diacetyl; possible blow-off
alarms.action: Open the side glycol valve, verify the setpoint profile, and check glycol supply

alarms.name: CEL.FV101.TT02.ALM_DEVIATION
alarms.cause: Cone glycol valve stuck or failed, or yeast cake insulating the cone RTD
alarms.consequence: Poor yeast settling and uneven crash; slower turnaround
alarms.action: Check the cone glycol valve and the cone RTD; compare with the side temperature

alarms.name: CEL.FV101.PT01.ALM_HIGH
alarms.cause: Spunding valve stuck closed or setpoint too high during active fermentation
alarms.consequence: Mechanical relief lifts at 15 psig MAWP (27.1 psia); CO2 release into the cellar
alarms.action: Reduce the spunding setpoint or vent manually; check the spunding valve

alarms.name: CEL.FV101.PT01.ALM_LOW
alarms.cause: CO2 reabsorption and gas contraction during cold crash without top pressure
alarms.consequence: Vacuum relief admits air; oxygen pickup and staling
alarms.action: Apply CO2 top pressure through the blow-off arm

alarms.name: CEL.BBT201.TT01.ALM_DEVIATION
alarms.cause: Jacket valve fault or warm glycol supply
alarms.consequence: Carbonation drifts off target and the beer warms
alarms.action: Check the BBT jacket valve and the glycol supply temperature

alarms.name: CEL.BBT201.PT01.ALM_HIGH
alarms.cause: Carbonation stone left open or regulator setpoint too high
alarms.consequence: Mechanical relief lifts at 15 psig; CO2 released into the cellar
alarms.action: Close the carbonation valve and vent to the target pressure

alarms.name: CEL.BBT202.TT01.ALM_DEVIATION
alarms.cause: Jacket valve fault or warm glycol supply
alarms.consequence: Carbonation drifts off target and the beer warms
alarms.action: Check the BBT jacket valve and the glycol supply temperature

alarms.name: CEL.BBT202.PT01.ALM_HIGH
alarms.cause: Carbonation stone left open or regulator setpoint too high
alarms.consequence: Mechanical relief lifts at 15 psig; CO2 released into the cellar
alarms.action: Close the carbonation valve and vent to the target pressure

alarms.name: CEL.SYS.XS01.ALM_STATE
alarms.cause: Cellar CO2 at or above 15,000 ppm (bas-vent tier 2)
alarms.consequence: BBT carbonation is held until the room is safe
alarms.action: Confirm the purge fans are running and find the CO2 source before re-entry
alarms.text: Carbonation inhibited by the cellar CO2 relay (plc-cellar interlock): state alarm

alarms.name: PKG.LINE.PACKML.ALM_STATE
alarms.cause: An upstream or downstream machine held the line (jam, starved, or blocked)
alarms.consequence: Lost production and warm product in the filler bowl
alarms.action: Check the PackML stop reason and clear the holding machine
alarms.text: Bottling line PackML state (StateCurrent): state alarm

alarms.name: PKG.FILLER.YA01.ALM_STATE
alarms.cause: Fallen bottle, broken glass, or label stock fault at the machine
alarms.consequence: The machine stops; the line blocks or starves
alarms.action: Clear the jam with the machine in Maintenance mode, then reset

alarms.name: PKG.FILLER.LSL01.ALM_STATE
alarms.cause: BBT pressure or level low, or the product valve closed
alarms.consequence: Short fills and foaming; rejects at fill-level inspection
alarms.action: Check BBT-202 pressure and level and the filler product valve
alarms.text: Filler bowl low (product supply): state alarm

alarms.name: PKG.RINSER.YA01.ALM_STATE
alarms.cause: Fallen bottle, broken glass, or label stock fault at the machine
alarms.consequence: The machine stops; the line blocks or starves
alarms.action: Clear the jam with the machine in Maintenance mode, then reset

alarms.name: PKG.CODER.YA01.ALM_STATE
alarms.cause: Fallen bottle, broken glass, or label stock fault at the machine
alarms.consequence: The machine stops; the line blocks or starves
alarms.action: Clear the jam with the machine in Maintenance mode, then reset

alarms.name: PKG.LABELER.YA01.ALM_STATE
alarms.cause: Fallen bottle, broken glass, or label stock fault at the machine
alarms.consequence: The machine stops; the line blocks or starves
alarms.action: Clear the jam with the machine in Maintenance mode, then reset

alarms.name: PKG.PACKER.YA01.ALM_STATE
alarms.cause: Fallen bottle, broken glass, or label stock fault at the machine
alarms.consequence: The machine stops; the line blocks or starves
alarms.action: Clear the jam with the machine in Maintenance mode, then reset

alarms.name: UTL.CHL.TT01.ALM_HIGH
alarms.cause: Chiller compressor fault, high load (crash plus knockout), or high ambient
alarms.consequence: Fermenters lose temperature control; batches at risk
alarms.action: Check the chiller stages and faults; defer cold crashes and knockout

alarms.name: UTL.CHL.YA01.ALM_STATE
alarms.cause: Compressor trip (high head pressure, low suction, or overload)
alarms.consequence: Glycol capacity drops; supply temperature rises
alarms.action: Reset the chiller at its controller; call for service if it repeats

alarms.name: UTL.GLY.LT01.ALM_LOW
alarms.cause: Glycol leak at a jacket, hose, or pump seal
alarms.consequence: Pump cavitation and loss of cooling
alarms.action: Find and isolate the leak; top up the reservoir with 35% propylene glycol

alarms.name: UTL.STM.PT01.ALM_LOW
alarms.cause: Boiler disabled, feeder open, or demand above 200 kW
alarms.consequence: Slow heating; the boil may not reach vigor
alarms.action: Check the boiler enable, its feeder breaker, and the steam demand

alarms.name: UTL.STM.LSL01.ALM_STATE
alarms.cause: Feedwater pump failure or a leak; the hardwired low-water cutoff tripped
alarms.consequence: Boiler off; no steam for mash, boil, or CIP
alarms.action: Check the feedwater supply and the cutoff; reset at the boiler
alarms.text: Boiler low-water cutoff tripped (hardwired): state alarm

alarms.name: UTL.AIR.PT01.ALM_LOW
alarms.cause: Compressor off or failed, or a large leak
alarms.consequence: Pneumatic valves and the bottling line stop
alarms.action: Check the compressor and the dryer; look for leaks

alarms.name: UTL.CO2.LT01.ALM_LOW
alarms.cause: Normal consumption since the last delivery
alarms.consequence: Supply runs out in a few days
alarms.action: Schedule a bulk CO2 delivery
alarms.text: Bulk CO2 tank level: low alarm

alarms.name: UTL.CO2.PT02.ALM_LOW
alarms.cause: Bulk tank low or vaporizer frozen
alarms.consequence: No CO2 for purging, carbonation, or counterpressure filling
alarms.action: Check the bulk tank level and the vaporizer; order a delivery
alarms.text: CO2 supply header pressure: low alarm

alarms.name: UTL.RO.AT01.ALM_HIGH
alarms.cause: RO membrane fouling or a failed carbon prefilter
alarms.consequence: Brewing liquor out of specification
alarms.action: Check the membranes and the carbon filter; switch to the backup supply

alarms.name: UTL.WWN.LT01.ALM_HIGH
alarms.cause: Discharge inhibited for a long time, or a large dump
alarms.consequence: Tank overflow to the floor drain (permit violation)
alarms.action: Stop CIP and brewhouse drains until the tank is neutralized and discharged

alarms.name: UTL.WWN.AT01.ALM_HIGH
alarms.cause: Caustic or acid CIP dump faster than the dosing can neutralize
alarms.consequence: Discharge inhibited until pH returns to 6.0-9.0
alarms.action: Check the dosing pumps and chemical levels; hold CIP dumps

alarms.name: UTL.WWN.AT01.ALM_LOW
alarms.cause: Caustic or acid CIP dump faster than the dosing can neutralize
alarms.consequence: Discharge inhibited until pH returns to 6.0-9.0
alarms.action: Check the dosing pumps and chemical levels; hold CIP dumps

alarms.name: UTL.WWN.XS01.ALM_STATE
alarms.cause: Neutralization tank pH outside 6.0-9.0
alarms.consequence: Tank fills; CIP and brewhouse drains must stop when it is full
alarms.action: Check the neutralization and dosing; do not override the discharge permit

alarms.name: UTL.CIP.TT01.ALM_DEVIATION
alarms.cause: Steam valve fault or low steam pressure
alarms.consequence: Caustic below 175 degF cleans poorly; the cycle must be repeated
alarms.action: Check the CIP steam valve and the steam header pressure

alarms.name: PWR.MAIN.JT01.ALM_HIGH
alarms.cause: Coincident boiler, chiller, and packaging load above the demand target
alarms.consequence: A new monthly demand peak costs about $37 per kW in summer
alarms.action: Defer the next boil step or packaging start; check the BESS dispatch
alarms.text: Service real power (import positive): high alarm

alarms.name: PWR.MAIN.ET01.ALM_LOW
alarms.cause: Utility voltage sag or heavy motor starting
alarms.consequence: Below ANSI C84.1 Range A; motors run hot and drives may trip
alarms.action: Check the utility service and the load; stagger motor starts
alarms.text: Service voltage, line to line: low alarm

alarms.name: PWR.MAIN.YA01.ALM_STATE
alarms.cause: Overcurrent or ground fault on the 480 V service
alarms.consequence: The whole site is on the genset (EP-1 only)
alarms.action: Do not reclose before the fault is found; call the electrical contractor

alarms.name: PWR.BESS.EY01.ALM_LOW
alarms.cause: Discharge for peak shaving or energy shift without enough recharge
alarms.consequence: Too little energy to cap the next brew-day peak
alarms.action: Check the overnight recharge schedule and the dispatch settings
alarms.text: BESS state of charge: low alarm

alarms.name: PWR.BESS.YA01.ALM_STATE
alarms.cause: PCS fault, battery temperature, or a communication loss
alarms.consequence: No peak shaving; the monthly demand peak may rise
alarms.action: Check the PCS fault code and reset it from its panel

alarms.name: PWR.GEN.ZS01.ALM_STATE
alarms.cause: Utility feeder lost (Summit Valley Power) or the main breaker opened
alarms.consequence: Brewhouse and packaging stop; EP-1 runs on the genset
alarms.action: Confirm the genset carries EP-1; hold the large feeders open until the utility returns
alarms.text: ATS on the emergency source: state alarm

alarms.name: FAC.RTU1.TT01.ALM_HIGH
alarms.cause: RTU-1 cooling stage fault or an economizer stuck open on a hot day
alarms.consequence: Uncomfortable taproom; guests leave
alarms.action: Check RTU-1 cooling stages and the economizer damper

alarms.name: FAC.CR.TT01.ALM_HIGH
alarms.cause: Door left open, defrost stuck, or condensing unit fault
alarms.consequence: Kegs warm; foaming at the taps and product quality loss
alarms.action: Close the door, check the defrost and the compressor

alarms.name: FAC.VENT.AT01.ALM_HIGH
alarms.cause: Fermentation venting, a CO2 leak, or the purge fans not running
alarms.consequence: CO2 above the NIOSH short-term limit (30,000 ppm) is near
alarms.action: Keep staff out of the cellar, confirm the purge fans, and find the source

alarms.name: FAC.VENT.AT01.ALM_HIGHHIGH
alarms.cause: Large CO2 release (blow-off, relief valve, or line break)
alarms.consequence: Life safety; CO2 at the NIOSH STEL and approaching IDLH (40,000 ppm)
alarms.action: Evacuate the cellar; enter only with SCBA; ventilate before re-entry
